## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Aññāsikoṇḍaññattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 9) is a verse text included in the *Therāpadāna* collection of the Pali canon [SuttaCentral]. The text recounts the past-life meritorious deeds and spiritual background of the senior disciple Aññāsi Koṇḍañña [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral records five translations of the poem into five modern languages [SuttaCentral].
While no direct canonical parallels are listed on SuttaCentral, automated analysis by DharmaNexus reveals substantial text reuse within Pali literature, identifying 97 matching passages across 18 Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. The most extensive reuse occurs in the commentary on the *Theragāthā* (*Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā*, Dutiyo bhāgo §2968–2999, which closely parallels segments 1.1–16.3 of this apadāna, as well as the Paṭhamo bhāgo) [DharmaNexus]. Furthermore, formulaic narrative segments (especially §17.1–19.1) recur across several other *Therāpadāna* poems, including the *Bhāgineyyupālittheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 43), *Rāhulattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 18), *Mahāmoggallānattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 4), and *Upālittheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 8) [DharmaNexus]. Cross-language alignments computed by DharmaNexus include matches with the Sanskrit *Kaṭhināvadāna* (aligning segments 15.3–16.2 with verses 326–327) and lower-scoring correspondences with the Tibetan *Ārya-ratnākara-nāma-mahāyāna-sūtra* (D0124) [DharmaNexus].
*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
